summary.text: 年 is first documented in Shang divination as a word for a harvest. Its early graph is interpreted as grain above a person; it later came to be used for a year, though the full path between these meanings is not dated.

formation.text: The earliest supported construction is pictographic: a grain plant 禾 above a human-shaped figure, interpreted as a person carrying grain in connection with harvest. A competing account assigns the lower element a phonetic role, but the evidence here does not establish that analysis. The traditional analysis of 禾 plus phonetic 千 is a later lexicographic account, not proof of the earliest structure.

components.text: 禾 is the upper grain plant. In the early graph it contributes to the depicted scene of grain carried by a person and is associated with the harvest meaning.
The lower figure is interpreted as a person, 人, carrying grain. One account proposes that it also supplied a sound cue, but that role is disputed and lacks a substantiated sound comparison here.

sound_limitation.text: A phonetic role is proposed in some accounts, but no usable comparison between 人 and 年 is established by the supplied evidence; the available 年 reconstruction alone cannot show that relationship.

history.text: The supplied oracle-bone rendering illustrates grain above a human-shaped figure. It is a modern redraw, not an artifact photograph, and illustrates an interpretation rather than proving the lower figure’s sound role.

Later accounts report a lower-element change from 人 to 千 and the Shuowen analysis “from 禾, with 千 as phonetic.” The character database describes the change as a misformation; the sequence has not been independently checked against a dated run of glyph images in this research.

The evidence also preserves a competing account in which 人 had both pictorial and phonetic functions. The harvest scene is supported, but the proposed sound function is not resolved by the available phonological evidence.

uncertainties.text: Whether the early lower element 人 also served as a phonetic component remains disputed. No supplied comparison establishes its historical reading in 年; the reconstruction supplied for 年 does not by itself identify a sound component.

The cited sources do not establish a complete dated sequence from harvest to recurring year, calendar year, New Year, or age. A grain-cycle-to-year extension is proposed, while other listed senses are documented without a full chronology.

senses.text: An oracle-bone divination asks whether the speaker will receive 年, interpreted as a good harvest; another cited Shang example is also read as harvest.

senses.period: Shang use is reported; later Western Zhou examples are cited
senses.text: A grain-cycle-to-year extension is proposed. A possible Shang time-count use is reported with an explicit caution about its reading, and Western Zhou bronze examples use 年 in wishes for long duration. These attestations do not date every step of the development.

senses.period: Shang and Zhou usage as described in the source; absolute dates unresolved
senses.text: A source distinguishes 年 as harvest, 歲 as harvest season, and 祀 as a regnal-year count in one Shang inscription; it reports that Zhou usage later replaced 祀 with 年 for regnal dating.
New Year is recorded as a later sense, but the supplied evidence does not date its emergence or establish its path from the harvest sense.
The character is used for a person's age. The supplied definitions document this sense but do not establish when or how it developed.

developments.text: The proposed link is that a successful grain cycle came to stand for a year. The sources do not establish the complete chronology.

limitations.text: The listed later senses are not all connected by sourced semantic developments; dictionary listings alone do not establish chronology.

overview.text: 年 first appears for harvest: the early graph is read as grain above a person carrying it. It later means “year,” though the evidence does not date the full transition.

components.text: 禾 is grain, shown above the person in the early harvest scene.
人 is read as the person carrying the grain; a proposed sound role remains unsettled.

relationships.text: In the early graph, 禾 is interpreted as grain carried by the person and contributes to the harvest scene.
The lower human-shaped element is interpreted as a person carrying grain; a separate proposed sound role is unresolved.
